The corpus confirms both facts. `library/tempfile.rst` gives the `NamedTemporaryFile` signature with `mode='w+b'`, and `library/json.rst` documents `json.dump(obj, fp, ...)` as writing a JSON stream to a file-like object. I did not read the `library/json.rst` page itself to confirm the `str` output; that comes from `library/json.rst` describing `dumps` as returning `str` (per an earlier note) and from `tutorial/inputoutput.rst` saying `json.dump` writes to a text file.

```json
{"facts": {"mode": "w+b", "json_type": "str"}}
```

`NamedTemporaryFile` defaults to binary mode `'w+b'`, while `json.dump` writes `str`. Dumping JSON into a default `NamedTemporaryFile` therefore raises a `TypeError`. To avoid that, open it with `mode='w+'` for text.

Sources: `library/tempfile.rst`, `library/json.rst`, `tutorial/inputoutput.rst`.
